602:
** ἀπο-κάλυψις** [κᾰ], εως, ἡ,
**uncovering,** of the head, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.38J.}}; **disclosing,** of hidden springs, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Aemilius Paulus” 14: _metaphorically_, ἁμαρτίας [prev. author] 2.7o f}}; **revelation,** especially of divine mysteries, {{NT|NT.Rom.16.25, etc.}}; of persons, **manifestation,** {{NT|NT.2Thes.1.7, etc.}}; title of **the Apocalypse.**
604:
** ἀποκαταλλάσσω**,
_Attic dialect_ **ἀποκαταλλάττω**, **reconcile again,** {{NT|NT.Eph.2.16}}; τὰ πάντα εἰς αὑτόν{{NT|NT.Col.1.20.}}
605:
** ἀποκατά-στᾰσις**, εως, ἡ,
**restoration, re-establishment,** τοῦ ἐνδεοῦς{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Magna Moralia” 1205a4; εἰς φύσιν [prev. work] 1204b36, 1205b11}}; **return to** a position, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Epistulae” 1p.8U.}}; especially of military formations, **reversal** of a movement, {{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 10.6, etc.; generally, πάντων NT.Act.3.21}}; of the soul, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 199 (_plural_); τῆς φύσιος ἐς τὸ ἀρχαῖον 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “χρονίων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 1.5}}; **recovery from sickness,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|[prev. author] “SA” 1.10; τῶν ὁμήρων εἰς τὰς πατρίδας 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.99.6}}; εἰς ἀ. ἐλθεῖν, of the affairs of a city, {{Refs|[prev. author] 4.23.1}}; **return** to original position, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Asclepiodotus Tacticus “Tact.” 10.1}}; ἀ. ἄστρων **return** of the stars to the same place in the heavens as in the former year, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.937f, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.36, etc.}}; **periodic return** of the cosmic cycle, {{Refs|“Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta” 2.184,190}}; of a planet, **return** to a place in the heavens occupied at a former epoch, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Antiochus Atheniensis Astrologus cited in “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 7.120,121}}; but, **zodiacal revolution,** {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Paulus Alexandrinus Astrologus “T.” 1}}; opposed to ἀνταπ. (which see), {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Dorotheus Astrologus cited in “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 2.196.9}}; **restoration** of sun and moon after eclipse, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370b.}}
607:
** ἀποκεφᾰλ-ίζω**,
**behead,** {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.1.24, LXX.Psa.151.7, variant in 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.35}}; of a fish, Dorioap.{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 7.287e}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ σημείων καὶ σημειώσεων” 13, 29, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.1.19.}}
616:
** ἀποκῠ-έω**,
**bear young, bring forth,** with _accusative_, {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 76, interpolated in 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 1.70, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Sulla” 37: _absolutely_, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 10.1: _metaphorically_, ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀ. θάνατον NT.Jam.1.15, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.214}}:—_passive_, of the child, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Lycurgus” 3. 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 1.5.5}} (_passive_ _participle_ ἀποκυόμενα{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.202, 397).}}
617:
** ἀπο-κῠλίω**,
**roll away,** {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Gen.29.3, +others, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 14.116, NT.Matt.28.2, 2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 3.15.7}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Rh.Pr.” 3.}}
621:
** ἀπολείχω**,
**lick off,** ἕλκη, variant for{ἐπι-}, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.478, cf. Epic. in “Arch.Papyrus” 7.6, 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 6.250a, Scholia 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” “Oxy.” 221ii33}} **lick clean,** with _genitive_ _partitive_, φόνου{{NT|NT.Luke.16.21.}}
623:
**Ἀπολλύων**, -οντος, ὁ
(present ptcp. of ἀπολλύω),
Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: Rev.9:11 (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; _DB_, i, 125, 172.) †
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
624:
**Ἀπολλωνία**, -ας, ἡ
**Apollonia, a city of Macedonia**: Act.17:1.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
625:
**Ἀπολλώς**, -ώ, ὁ
(perh. contr. from Ἀπολλώνιος, Act.18:24 D)
**Apollos**: Act.18:24 19:1, 1Co.1:12 3:4-6 3:22 4:6 16:12, Tit.3:13.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
627:
** ἀπολογ-ία**, ἡ,
**speech in defence,** opposed to κατηγορία, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.7, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.61, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 28a, etc.}}; ἀ. ποιεῖσθαι to make **a defence,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.62; ἀ. ποιεῖσθαι τὸν ἑαυτοῦ βίον τῶν τοῦ πατρὸς ἀδικημάτων 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 14.29; τῶν κατηγορηθέντων τὸ μὴ λαβὸν ἀπολογίαν 4th c.BC: Hyperides Orator “pro Euxenippo” 31; ἀ. τοῦ εὐαγγελίου NT.Phil.1.16}}; explanation by πληροφορία, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}
636:
** ἀποπλέω**,
_Epic dialect_ **ἀποπλείω**, _Ionic dialect_ **ἀποπλώω** see reading in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.156, 157, compare 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Indica” 26.9}}: _future_ **-πλεύσομαι**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.147}} **-πλευσοῦμαι** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Mi.” 371b}}:— **sail away, sail off,** οἴκαδ᾽ ἀποπλείειν{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.418, etc.; ἐπ᾽ Αἰγύπτου 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1480; ὀπίσω ἀ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.156; ἐκ τῆς Σικελίας ὡς ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.61; ἐπ᾽ οἴκου [prev. author] 1.55.}}
642:
** ἀπορφᾰνίζω**,
**bereave,** τινὰ παιδός{{Refs|“BCH” 46.345}}:—_passive_, **to be orphaned,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 249}}; ἀπό τινος ἀ. **to be torn away from..,**{{NT|NT.1Thes.2.17.}}
655:
** ἀποστῠγ-έω**,
_aorist 1_ **-εστύγησα**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 692}}(Lyric poetry), **-έστυξα** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Oppianus Anazarbensis Epicus “Halieutica - Poetae Bucolici et Didactici” 4.370}}: _aorist 2_ ἀπέστῠγον{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Callimachus Epicus “Aetia” 1.1.11, “Del.” 223, 2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “Alexipharmaca” 406, 1st c.BC: Parthenius Mythographus 36.2}}: _perfect_ with _present_ sense, **-εστύγηκα**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.47}}:—**hate violently, abhor,** Hdt.[same place], {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 186, 692, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 488 (Lyric poetry in 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus and 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus)}}; ἀ. ὕδωρ (in comparison with wine) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Melanippides Lyricus 4; ἄμυστιν Callias Epigrammaticus “Aet.”}}[same place]: with _infinitive_, ἀ. γαμβρὸν ἄν οἱ γενέσθαι Ἱπποκλείδεα{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.129.}}
656:
** ἀποσυν-άγωγος** [ᾰγ], ον,
**expelled from the synagogue,** {{NT|NT.John.9.22, etc.}}
660:
** ἀποτιν-άσσω** [ῐ],
**shake off,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 253}}:—_middle_, ἀποτινάξασθαι{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.821}}; ἀποτετίνακται τὸ ῥῆμα τῶν ὄνων **has got rid of** it, {{LXX|LXX.1Ki.10.2.}}
662:
** ἀποτολμ-άω**,
**make a bold venture upon,** τινί{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.67}}: with _infinitive_, ἀ. ἐπιχειρῆσαι{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.28; λέγειν 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.131, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 2.45.2, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.233, etc.:}} —_perfect_ _participle_ _passive_ in _active_ sense, δι᾽ ἐλευθερίας λίαν ἀποτετολμημένης too **presumptuous** liberty, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 701b, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Galba” 25: in _passive_ sense, εἰπεῖν τὰ νῦν ἀποτετ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 503b: _absolutely_, ἀποτολμᾷ καὶ λέγει NT.Rom.10.20: with _accusative_, ἀναίρεσιν 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 7.8.3.}}
670:
** ἀποφορτ-ίζομαι**,
_middle_, **discharge one's cargo,** τὸν γόμον{{NT|NT.Act.21.3}}; **jettison,** _absolutely_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.413; τῇ θαλάσσῃ τὰ περιττὰ τῶν φορτίων 4th-3rd c.BC: Timaeus Historicus 61}}; **unload one's stomach,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 2.26:}} —_passive_, of περιττώματα, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.40}}: generally, **jettison, get rid of,** τι {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.434, etc.}}
675:
**Ἀππιος**, -ου, ὁ
**Appius**; Ἀππίου Φόρον, Appii Forum (Market of Appius), **a town in Italy**: Act.28:15.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
676:
** ἀπρόσ-ῐτος**, ον,
**unapproachable, inaccessible,** ὄρη{{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.49.7, compare 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.3.18; φῶς NT.1Tim.6.16}}; of persons, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 5.20.6, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.68e; καταφυγή 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.96: _metaphorically_, λόγοις ἀ. παρρησία 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alcibiades” 4; δύναμις τοῦ λόγου 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Dem.Enc.” 32}}. _adverb_ **-τως**{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.45f.}}
678:
Included with: ** ἀπροσωπόληπτος**, ον,
**not respecting persons,** [{{Refs|10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see {ἀδυσώπητος}}}]. _adverb_ **-τως** **without respect of persons,** {{NT|NT.1Pet.1.17.}}
682:
**Ἀπφία**, -ας, ἡ
**Apphia**: Phm 2 (MM, see word).†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
688:
** Ἀρᾰβ-ία**, ἡ,
**Arabia,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.8, etc.}} (also, ={κόσμος γυναικός}, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus): poetry Ἀρραβία 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 17.86}}:—_adjective_ Ἀράβιος, α, ον, **Arabian,** οἱ Ἀ.{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.198, +others}}:—also Ἀραβικός, ή, όν, χάραγμα{{Refs 1st c.AD+|“PGen.” 29.8 (2nd c.AD), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 69, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}}:—later Ἄραβες (see. Ἄραψ):—peculiar _feminine_ Ἀραβίς, ίδος, {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 34.56: Ἀράβισσα, 5th c.AD(?): Stephanus Byzantius}}
689:

**Aram**: Mat.1:3-4, Luk.3:33 (R, txt., WH, Ἀρνεί).†

690:
** Ἄραψ**, ὁ,
_plural_ Ἄραβες, οἱ, **Arab,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 1.2.34, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 1.19.4:}} —as _adjective_, Ἄραψ ἀτμός, of incense, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“Paean Delphicus [2nd c.BC]” 11; θώρηξ 4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 36.326: _dative_ _plural_ Ἀράβεσσι [prev. work] 26.23.}}
